scheme_name: Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)
description:
The Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture also known as HRT-2 was launched by the Government of India in the year 2014. 

This scheme aims to promote holistic growth and development in the horticulture sector across the country. 

The initiative is part of the National Horticulture Mission which was initially launched in 2005. 

The primary objective of HRT-2 is to enhance the production of horticultural crops in a sustainable manner. 

The scheme targets an increase in the area under horticulture crops by approximately 20 percent over the next five years. 

The program also aims to improve the income of farmers involved in horticulture by at least 30 percent. 

One of the specific goals is to increase the export of horticultural products by 50 percent by the year 2025. 

The scheme focuses on various horticultural crops including fruits, vegetables, flowers, and spices. 

It also aims to promote the use of modern technologies in horticulture practices. 

The benefits under this scheme include financial assistance for various horticulture activities. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 1.5 lakh per hectare for the establishment of new orchards. 

For the cultivation of vegetables, farmers can receive assistance of INR 75,000 per hectare. 

The scheme also provides support for the construction of polyhouses with a maximum subsidy of 50 percent of the cost. 

For the establishment of a polyhouse, the maximum subsidy can be up to INR 1.5 lakh. 

Additionally, the scheme provides assistance for the development of irrigation facilities. 

Farmers can receive up to 80 percent of the cost for installing drip irrigation systems. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of post-harvest management. 

Financial assistance is available for setting up packhouses and cold storage facilities. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 50 lakh for establishing cold storage units. 

The eligibility criteria for the HRT-2 scheme include being a resident of India. 

Farmers must be engaged in horticulture activities for at least three years. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There are no specific income criteria mentioned for eligibility. 

Educational qualifications are not a prerequisite for applying to the scheme. 

The application process for the HRT-2 scheme is straightforward. 

Farmers need to visit the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

They must fill out the application form available online. 

Required documents include proof of residence, land ownership documents, and identity proof. 

Farmers must also provide details of the horticulture activities they are engaged in. 

After submitting the application, it will be reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

Once approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the applicant. 

The timeline for application submission is generally open throughout the year. 

However, specific deadlines may be set for certain activities or projects. 

The disbursement of funds typically occurs within 30 days of approval. 

The implementing authority for the HRT-2 scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Horticulture Board is also involved in the execution of the scheme. 

State horticulture departments play a crucial role in the implementation at the state level. 

Farmers can contact the local horticulture department for assistance with the application process. 

The contact details for the Ministry of Agriculture can be found on their official website. 

The scheme also aims to promote organic farming practices among horticulturists. 

Financial assistance is available for farmers transitioning to organic farming. 

Up to 50 percent of the cost of organic inputs can be reimbursed under the scheme. 

The HRT-2 scheme also includes training programs for farmers. 

These programs are designed to educate farmers about modern horticulture practices. 

Workshops and seminars are conducted regularly to disseminate knowledge. 

The scheme encourages the formation of farmer producer organizations. 

These organizations help in collective marketing of horticultural produce. 

The government aims to increase the participation of women in horticulture through this scheme. 

Special provisions are made to encourage women farmers to apply for assistance. 

The scheme also focuses on enhancing the quality of horticultural produce. 

Quality control measures are implemented to ensure that the produce meets market standards. 

The HRT-2 scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It aims to generate at least 1 million jobs in the horticulture sector by 2025. 

The scheme is aligned with the broader goals of the National Policy for Farmers. 

It aims to increase the income of farmers and improve their livelihoods. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 2,000 crore for the implementation of the HRT-2 scheme. 

This budget is intended to support various activities under the scheme over a five-year period. 

The scheme is expected to significantly contribute to the agricultural GDP of India. 

It aims to enhance the overall economic development of rural areas. 

The HRT-2 scheme is a vital component of India's agricultural strategy. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the horticulture sector. 

The scheme is expected to benefit millions of farmers across the country. 

The government encourages all eligible farmers to take advantage of this scheme. 

By participating in HRT-2, farmers can improve their productivity and income levels. 

The scheme is a step towards achieving food security and nutritional security in India. 

Overall, the Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses various challenges faced by the horticulture sector in India. 

The scheme aims to create a sustainable and profitable horticulture industry. 

Farmers are encouraged to engage with local authorities for more information. 

The government is committed to supporting the growth of horticulture in India. 

The HRT-2 scheme is a significant opportunity for farmers to enhance their livelihoods.
